body:
## Problem

The lockfile the release pipeline installs from pins 9 packages with 24 published advisories (1 Critical, 12 High, 11 Medium). The in-progress dependency bump in the working tree (package.json + yarn.lock, both modified) does not clear any of them: the scan below ran against the modified lock.

## Evidence

`osv-scanner scan source --lockfile=yarn.lock` against the current working-tree lock:

```
Total 9 packages affected by 24 known vulnerabilities
(1 Critical, 12 High, 11 Medium, 0 Low) from 1 ecosystem.
24 vulnerabilities can be fixed.

tar              7.5.16  -> 7.5.19  GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw  CVSS 9.2
tar              7.5.16  -> 7.5.18  GHSA-8x88-c5mf-7j5w  CVSS 8.7
brace-expansion  5.0.6   -> 5.0.9   GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895  CVSS 7.5
fast-uri         3.1.2   -> 3.1.5   GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7  CVSS 7.5
js-yaml          4.2.0   -> 4.3.1   GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj  CVSS 7.5
ip-address       10.2.0  -> 10.3.1  GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr  CVSS 7.7
sigstore         4.1.0   -> 4.1.1   GHSA-52v5-jr5w-gjxr  CVSS 7.5
@sigstore/verify 3.1.0   -> 3.1.1   GHSA-xgjw-pm74-86q4  CVSS 6.5
@sigstore/core   3.1.0   -> 3.2.1   GHSA-jfc7-64v2-mr8c  CVSS 5.4
undici           8.5.0                                   (also flagged)
```

`package.json:47-51` already pins three of these by intent, and the pins have gone stale:

```json
"resolutions": {
  "brace-expansion": "^5.0.6",
  "picomatch": "^4.0.4",
  "undici": "^8.0.0"
}
```

`git log` shows the same packages being patched repeatedly for security and drifting back — `5285c6c chore(deps): update dependency undici (8.0.2 → 8.5.0) [security]`, `06002e7 chore(deps): bump brace-expansion`, `51ecf11 chore(deps): bump tar`.

## Impact

`.github/workflows/publish.yml` installs from this lock and then runs `cycjimmy/semantic-release-action` in the `release` environment holding `secrets.PAT` and npm OIDC publish rights (`id-token: write`). `tar`, `sigstore`, `@sigstore/verify` and `@sigstore/core` are all on the semantic-release/npm-publish path, so the Critical archive-handling flaw sits directly inside the privileged publishing job. `js-yaml` and `brace-expansion` reach through `@commitlint/cli`, which this package declares as a runtime `dependency`.

## Fix

Refresh the transitives and re-verify:

```sh
yarn up -R tar js-yaml brace-expansion fast-uri ip-address undici sigstore @sigstore/core @sigstore/verify
osv-scanner scan source --lockfile=yarn.lock   # must report 0
```

Then add a gating scan so the lock cannot drift silently again — a step in `.github/workflows/test.yml` after checkout:

```yaml
      - name: Scan lockfile
        uses: google/osv-scanner-action/osv-scanner-action@<pinned-sha>
        with:
          scan-args: |-
            --lockfile=yarn.lock
```

## Resolution
Ran `yarn up -R tar js-yaml brace-expansion fast-uri ip-address undici sigstore @sigstore/core @sigstore/verify`. `osv-scanner scan source --lockfile=yarn.lock` now reports "No issues found" across 457 packages, down from 24 vulnerabilities in 9 packages. brace-expansion moved 5.0.6 -> 5.0.9 under the existing `^5.0.6` resolution, confirming the pins were correct and only the lock was stale. Added a gating `lockfile` job to .github/workflows/test.yml running google/osv-scanner-action pinned to 8deb546 (v2.5.0, SHA verified against the GitHub tags API) so the drift fails CI instead of surfacing at release time. The CI job itself has not been executed on GitHub — only the local scan is verified.
title: Committed yarn.lock carries 24 known vulnerabilities including a CVSS 9.2 in tar

body:
## Problem

`package.json` declares `engines: { "node": ">=20" }`, but both runtime dependencies declare `>=22.12.0`. The published support floor is a promise the package cannot keep, and nothing in CI ever exercises it.

## Evidence

`package.json:13-15` and `package.json:44-46`:

```json
"engines": { "node": ">=20" },
"dependencies": {
  "@commitlint/cli": "^21.2.2",
  "@commitlint/config-conventional": "^21.2.2",
  "@ivuorinen/config-checker": "^2.6.7"
}
```

Resolved from the installed tree:

```
$ node -e "..."
this pkg engines.node = >=20
@commitlint/cli -> {"node":">=22.12.0"}
@commitlint/config-conventional -> {"node":">=22.12.0"}
```

Nothing tests the claim: `.nvmrc` is `26.4.0`, and `.github/workflows/test.yml:36-39` runs a single job on `node-version-file: ".nvmrc"` with no version matrix. Node 20 has never been executed against this package.

## Impact

A consumer on Node 20 or 21 runs `npm i -D @ivuorinen/commitlint-config`, sees this package's `engines` accept their runtime, and then gets `EBADENGINE` warnings from the two `@commitlint/*` packages — or a hard install failure under `engine-strict=true` / `--engine-strict`, or under pnpm, which enforces `engines` by default. If they push past the warning, commitlint itself will not run. The package advertises support for a runtime on which it is non-functional.

## Fix

Raise the floor to match reality in `package.json`:

```json
"engines": {
  "node": ">=22.12.0"
}
```

and make the claim testable by adding a matrix to `.github/workflows/test.yml` so the declared floor is actually run:

```yaml
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node-version: ["22.12.0", "24", "26"]
    steps:
      # ...
      - name: Setup Node.js Environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@48b55a011bda9f5d6aeb4c2d9c7362e8dae4041e # v6.4.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
```

(Dropping `node-version-file: ".nvmrc"` in favour of the matrix; `.nvmrc` stays the developer default.)

## Resolution
Raised `engines.node` to `">=22.12.0"`, matching what @commitlint/cli and @commitlint/config-conventional both require. Made the claim testable: .github/workflows/test.yml now runs a `fail-fast: false` matrix over Node 22.12.0, 24 and 26 instead of a single `.nvmrc` job, with a comment tying the matrix floor to engines.node. README states the requirement. The matrix has not been executed on GitHub; locally the suite passes on Node 26.4.0.
title: engines.node ">=20" is two majors below what both direct dependencies require

body:
## Problem

`NPM_TOKEN` is set in the workflow-level `env:` block, so it is injected into the environment of every step in the job — `actions/checkout`, the third-party `Simek/yarn-lock-changes` action, and the composite `ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint`. No step in this workflow publishes to npm or reads a private registry.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml:16-18`:

```yaml
env:
  NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
  GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
```

It is then re-injected per step at lines 51-53 and 58-60:

```yaml
      - name: Yarn Lock Changes
        uses: Simek/yarn-lock-changes@59f47ee499424d2c2437c5aebf863b5c6d50a5bc # v0.14.1
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

Confirmed independently by semgrep (`p/github-actions`), the only result across the whole repository:

```
yaml.github-actions.security.gha-workflow-env-secret .github/workflows/pr-lint.yml:17
A secret is exposed in the workflow-level `env:` block, making it available to
every job and step in this workflow
```

The job never runs an install or a publish — its only steps are checkout, `corepack enable`, the lock-diff comment action, and MegaLinter via `ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint`.

## Impact

A publish-capable npm token is placed in the process environment of two actions that have no use for it. `Simek/yarn-lock-changes` is third-party code; the SHA pin (`59f47ee…`) fixes what runs today but does not constrain what that code does with the environment it is handed. Any `env`-dumping debug output, crash reporter, or future compromise of a pinned-then-repinned dependency turns a lint job into an npm credential disclosure. The `environment: pr-lint` gate scopes *which jobs* can request the secret; it does nothing to narrow which steps inside the job see it.

## Fix

Delete the workflow-level `env:` block (lines 16-18) and the two `NPM_TOKEN` step entries. `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` at workflow level is also redundant — `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` and `github.token` are the same value, and the steps already pass it explicitly. The job becomes:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Deny-by-default at the workflow level; the job grants only what it needs.
permissions: {}

jobs:
  Linter:
    # ...
      - name: Yarn Lock Changes
        uses: Simek/yarn-lock-changes@59f47ee499424d2c2437c5aebf863b5c6d50a5bc # v0.14.1
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

If nothing then needs `NPM_TOKEN`, drop the `environment: pr-lint` line too — the environment exists only to scope that secret.

## Resolution
Deleted the workflow-level `env:` block from .github/workflows/pr-lint.yml and both step-level NPM_TOKEN entries. `Simek/yarn-lock-changes` and `ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint` now receive only `token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` via `with:`. Dropped the redundant `token:` from actions/checkout (github.token is the default) and the `environment: pr-lint` line, which existed only to scope the npm secret. Left a comment on the `permissions: {}` block recording why there is no workflow-level env. Verified: semgrep p/github-actions now returns 0 results across the repository, and actionlint is clean.
title: NPM_TOKEN is exposed to every step of the PR Lint job, including a third-party action

body:
## Problem

`pre-commit run --all-files` fails on `main` with nothing modified. Two hooks rewrite files that are already committed, so the repository does not satisfy its own hook configuration.

## Evidence

Run against a clean tree at `c3b77b3`:

```
pretty format json.......................................................Failed
- hook id: pretty-format-json
- exit code: 1
- files were modified by this hook

Fixing file .github/renovate.json
Fixing file .commitlintrc.json
Fixing file .releaserc.json

markdownlint.............................................................Failed
- hook id: markdownlint
- files were modified by this hook

PRECOMMIT_EXIT=1
```

Two independent causes.

**1. `pretty-format-json` and Prettier disagree on single-element arrays.** `.pre-commit-config.yaml:18-19` runs `pretty-format-json --autofix --no-sort-keys`, which always expands arrays one element per line:

```diff
 {
-  "extends": ["./index.cjs"]
+  "extends": [
+    "./index.cjs"
+  ]
 }
```

`.mega-linter.yml:25` enables `JSON_PRETTIER`, and Prettier collapses that same array back to one line. The two configured formatters revert each other on every pass, and the committed files are in Prettier's form.

**2. `markdownlint --fix` rewrites the generated CHANGELOG.** `.pre-commit-config.yaml:24-25` runs with `--fix`, which strips the double blank line semantic-release emits before each `### Bug Fixes` heading:

```diff
 ## [1.0.32](.../compare/v1.0.31...v1.0.32) (2026-06-25)
 
-
 ### Bug Fixes
```

`CHANGELOG.md` is regenerated by `@semantic-release/changelog` on every release, so this reappears after every publish. `.markdownlintignore` lists `node_modules/` and `docs/audit/` but not `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Impact

Any contributor who installs the hooks — which the config exists to encourage — has their first commit fail and then silently expanded to three unrelated JSON reformats plus a CHANGELOG edit. That noise lands in the diff of an unrelated PR. Because cause 2 regenerates on every release, the failure is permanent rather than one-time: fixing the CHANGELOG by hand today reintroduces the failure at the next `chore(release)` commit. The hooks are also non-gating — no workflow runs `pre-commit` — so the drift is invisible until someone runs it locally.

## Fix

Resolve the formatter conflict by dropping the one that loses. Prettier owns JSON style here (`.mega-linter.yml` runs it in CI; `pretty-format-json` runs nowhere but locally), so remove the hook from `.pre-commit-config.yaml:18-19`:

```yaml
      - id: mixed-line-ending
        args: [--fix=auto]
```

(delete the `pretty-format-json` entry)

Exempt the generated changelog in `.markdownlintignore`:

```text
node_modules/
docs/audit/
CHANGELOG.md
```

Then make the hooks gating so this cannot drift again — add to `.github/workflows/test.yml`:

```yaml
  pre-commit:
    name: Pre-commit hooks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read # required to checkout the repository
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pre-commit/action@2c7b3805fd2a0fd8c1884dcaebf91fc102a13ecd # v3.0.1
```

Verify with `pre-commit run --all-files && git diff --exit-code`.

## Resolution
Both causes addressed. Removed the `pretty-format-json` hook from .pre-commit-config.yaml with a comment recording that Prettier (JSON_PRETTIER in .mega-linter.yml) owns JSON style because it is the one that runs in CI. Added CHANGELOG.md to .markdownlintignore, since @semantic-release/changelog regenerates the blank lines markdownlint --fix strips. Also fixed two over-long README lines the new documentation introduced. Verified: `pre-commit run --all-files` exits 0 with every hook passing and `git status --porcelain` showing no hook-induced changes. Added a gating `pre-commit` job to .github/workflows/test.yml (pre-commit/action pinned to 2c7b3805, v3.0.1, SHA verified) so the drift cannot recur unnoticed; that job has not been executed on GitHub.

Note: reproducing this finding during the audit left the working tree dirty; .commitlintrc.json, .github/renovate.json, .releaserc.json and CHANGELOG.md were restored to their committed content before any fixes were applied.
title: pre-commit fails on a clean checkout: two hooks rewrite committed files

body:
## Problem

The `exports` map declares only `import` and `require`. Adding an `exports` field switches the package to strict encapsulation, so every subpath that is not listed becomes unreachable — including `./package.json`, which tooling routinely reads.

## Evidence

`package.json:18-21`:

```json
"exports": {
  "import": "./wrapper.mjs",
  "require": "./index.cjs"
}
```

Reproduced:

```
$ node -e "require('@ivuorinen/commitlint-config/package.json')"
ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED Package subpath './package.json' is not defined
by "exports" in .../package.json
```

There is also no `default` condition, so any resolver whose condition set does not include `import` or `require` finds no match at all. Node itself always supplies one of the two, but bundlers and alternative resolvers using their own condition lists (Metro's `react-native`, `browser`-first configurations) do not.

## Impact

Version-detection and config-introspection code — the common `require("@ivuorinen/commitlint-config/package.json").version` pattern, and tools that inspect a shareable config's manifest — throws instead of reading. `sideEffects` and metadata lookups by bundlers fail the same way. The failure mode is an opaque `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` rather than a missing file.

## Fix

Expose the manifest and add a fallback condition. Order matters — `default` must come last:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./wrapper.mjs",
    "require": "./index.cjs",
    "default": "./index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

`package.json` is already in the published tarball (`npm pack --dry-run` lists it), so no `files` change is needed.

## Resolution
Rewrote the `exports` map to the subpath form: `"."` carrying import/require/default, and `"./package.json": "./package.json"`. Verified `require("@ivuorinen/commitlint-config/package.json").version` returns 1.0.33 where it previously threw ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, and the existing CJS/ESM resolution tests still pass. Locked in by a new test case in test/resolve.test.mjs.
title: exports map blocks ./package.json and has no default condition

body:
## Problem

The README explains how to install the package but not what it configures. The one rule this package adds on top of `@commitlint/config-conventional` is undocumented, and the sentence describing the postinstall behaviour omits the condition that governs it.

## Evidence

`index.cjs:3-8` is the entire product, and its differentiating rule appears nowhere in the README:

```js
module.exports = {
  extends: ["@commitlint/config-conventional"],
  rules: {
    "body-leading-blank": [2, "always"],
  },
};
```

The upstream default is level 1 (warning); this package raises it to level 2 (error):

```
$ node -e "... require('@commitlint/config-conventional') ..."
body-leading-blank default: [1,"always"]
```

Verified end to end — a body without a leading blank line is an error, not a warning, under this config:

```
$ printf 'feat: subject\nbody without blank line\n' | npx commitlint --config .commitlintrc.json
✖   body must have leading blank line [body-leading-blank]
✖   found 1 problems, 0 warnings
```

`README.md:27` states the postinstall behaviour unconditionally:

> After installing it, a `.commitlintrc.json` file will be created automatically in the project's root folder

`scripts/postinstall.cjs:18-23` shows it is conditional — when `checkConfig("commitlint")` finds any existing commitlint config, the script logs and exits without writing. Neither that skip nor the `--ignore-scripts` opt-out is mentioned.

## Impact

A user comparing this package against plain `@commitlint/config-conventional` has no way to see what they gain, and the difference is a stricter failure level that will reject commits their previous setup accepted. A user whose existing config is silently left in place reads the README and concludes the install is broken.

## Fix

Add a section after Installation in `README.md`, and add it to the Table of Contents at `README.md:9-13`:

```markdown
## Configuration

Extends [`@commitlint/config-conventional`][config-conventional-link] with one
override:

| Rule | This config | `config-conventional` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `body-leading-blank` | `[2, "always"]` — error | `[1, "always"]` — warning |

A commit body that does not start with a blank line fails the lint here,
where upstream only warns.
```

and correct `README.md:27`:

```markdown
After installing it, a _`.commitlintrc.json`_ file is created in the project's
root folder with the configuration below — unless a commitlint config already
exists, in which case the existing one is left untouched. Install with
`--ignore-scripts` to skip this step entirely.
```

Add the link definition alongside the others at the bottom of the file:

```markdown
[config-conventional-link]: https://github.com/conventional-changelog/commitlint/tree/master/@commitlint/config-conventional
```

## Resolution
Added a "Configuration" section to README.md with a table contrasting `body-leading-blank` at `[2, "always"]` against config-conventional's `[1, "always"]`, stating that a body without a leading blank line fails here where upstream warns, and naming the Node >=22.12.0 floor. Corrected the postinstall sentence to state the skip-if-config-exists condition and the `--ignore-scripts` opt-out. Table of Contents updated. The documented behaviour is now enforced by the end-to-end commitlint test rather than only asserted in prose.
title: README never states what the config does, and describes the postinstall inaccurately

body:
## Problem

`.yamlignore` is a committed zero-byte file, and `.yamllint.yml` declares no `ignore:` key. Nothing excludes `node_modules`, so running yamllint the documented way reports third-party findings.

## Evidence

`.yamlignore` is 0 lines (`git ls-files | xargs wc -l` reports `0 .yamlignore`), and `.yamllint.yml` has no `ignore` key:

```yaml
extends: default

rules:
  line-length:
    max: 200
    level: warning
  truthy:
    check-keys: false
  comments:
    min-spaces-from-content: 1
  trailing-spaces:
    level: warning
```

A direct run:

```
$ yamllint -c .yamllint.yml .
./.yarnrc.yml
  1:1  warning  missing document start "---"  (document-start)
./node_modules/.yarn-state.yml
  1:1  warning  missing document start "---"  (document-start)
./node_modules/json-schema-traverse/.eslintrc.yml
./node_modules/err-code/.travis.yml
./node_modules/minimist/.github/FUNDING.yml
./node_modules/socks/.prettierrc.yaml
  7:22  error  no new line character at the end of file  (new-line-at-end-of-file)
  ... 13 files total
```

Only one of those findings is this repository's: `.yarnrc.yml:1` is missing the `---` document start that every other YAML file here carries. The rest are dependencies.

The pre-commit hook masks the problem because pre-commit passes only git-tracked files, so `.pre-commit-config.yaml:27-30` reports `yamllint ... Passed` while a bare run does not.

## Impact

The signal-to-noise ratio makes a direct `yamllint .` unusable: one real finding buried under 13 dependency files, including an `error`-level one that is not this repository's to fix. `.yamlignore` exists to prevent exactly this and, being empty, is dead weight that reads as though the problem were already handled.

## Fix

yamllint does not read `.yamlignore` — it reads the `ignore` key from its own config. Delete the empty file and put the exclusion where the tool looks, in `.yamllint.yml`:

```yaml
---
extends: default

ignore: |
  node_modules/
  .yarn/

rules:
  line-length:
    max: 200
    level: warning
  truthy:
    check-keys: false
  comments:
    min-spaces-from-content: 1
  trailing-spaces:
    level: warning
```

Then fix the one genuine finding by adding the document start to `.yarnrc.yml`:

```yaml
---
nodeLinker: node-modules
```

Verify with `yamllint -c .yamllint.yml .` — expected output is empty.

## Resolution
Deleted the empty .yamlignore and moved the exclusion to where yamllint actually reads it — an `ignore:` key in .yamllint.yml covering node_modules/ and .yarn/, with a comment recording that yamllint does not read .yamlignore. Also added the missing `---` document start to .yarnrc.yml, the one genuine finding the node_modules noise had been burying. Verified: `yamllint -c .yamllint.yml .` now produces no output at all, down from 13 files of findings including an error-level one.
title: .yamlignore is empty and yamllint has no ignore rule, so a direct run walks node_modules

body:
## Problem

`.gitignore` covers PHP/Laravel, Composer, PHPUnit, Vagrant, Homestead, Next.js, Vercel, Nuxt, Docusaurus, JetBrains IDEs and Crashlytics for a package whose entire source is three files. One line is also syntactically wrong: git does not support trailing comments.

## Evidence

`.gitignore:70`:

```text
!*.svg  # comment out if you don't need vector files
```

Git treats `#` as a comment only at the start of a line. The whole line is read as a single negation pattern, `!*.svg  # comment out if you dont need vector files`, which matches no file that will ever exist. The negation is dead twice over — nothing in the file ignores `*.svg` for it to re-include:

```
$ git check-ignore -v --no-index test.svg
$ echo $?
1                     # not ignored; the negation has no rule to negate
```

The surrounding entries are for stacks this repository does not use — `composer.phar`, `/vendor/`, `.phpunit.result.cache`, `bootstrap/compiled.php`, `Homestead.yaml`, `/.vagrant`, `atlassian-ide-plugin.xml`, `com_crashlytics_export_strings.xml`, `next-env.d.ts`, `.vercel`. The repository is six source files plus config.

Several rules are also duplicated with inconsistent anchoring: `node_modules/` (line 30) and `/node_modules`; `coverage` and `/coverage`; `out` and `out/`; `.cache` and `.cache/`; `build/Release`, `/build/` and `/build`; `npm-debug.log*` and `npm-debug.log`.

## Impact

Line 70 is a comment that is not a comment — a reader following its instruction to "comment out" a line that is already inert learns nothing, and anyone copying this file into a project that *does* ignore SVGs inherits a negation that silently does not work. The surrounding 120 lines of foreign-stack patterns make the file unreviewable: a genuinely wrong entry cannot be spotted among rules for tools the project has never used.

## Fix

Replace the file with what this repository actually produces:

```text
# Dependencies
node_modules/

# Yarn (node-modules linker; see .yarnrc.yml)
.yarn/cache
.yarn/unplugged
.yarn/build-state.yml
.yarn/install-state.gz
.pnp.*

# Build and test artefacts
*.tgz
coverage/
*.log

# Environment and editor
.env
.env*.local
.DS_Store
.idea/
```

Every removed entry corresponds to a tool this project does not use; `git status` on a clean tree must stay empty after the change, which is the check.

## Resolution
Replaced .gitignore with a 23-line file covering only what this repository produces: node_modules, the Yarn state paths implied by .yarnrc.yml's node-modules linker, *.tgz/coverage/*.log, .env files, and editor/OS artefacts. Removed the malformed `!*.svg  # comment out...` line — git has no trailing comments, so it was a single dead pattern — along with all PHP/Laravel/Composer/PHPUnit/Vagrant/Homestead/Next.js/Vercel/Nuxt/Docusaurus/JetBrains/Crashlytics entries and the duplicated anchoring variants. Verified `git status --porcelain` lists no newly untracked files after the change.
title: .gitignore is 134 lines of unrelated boilerplate with a malformed trailing comment

## Problem

`publish.yml` triggers only on `push` to `main`, but its `Linter` gate grants write scopes for pull requests and issues — objects that do not exist in a push event's context. The workflow is otherwise carefully deny-by-default, which makes these two grants the outliers.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/publish.yml:4-7` — push only, no `pull_request`:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
```

`.github/workflows/publish.yml:18-32` — the gate job and its scopes:

```yaml
  Linter:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      statuses: write # required to report the lint status
      contents: read # required to checkout the repository
      packages: read # required to read packages metadata
      issues: write # required for the linter to comment on issues
      pull-requests: write # required to comment on pull requests

    steps:
      - name: Run PR Lint
        uses: ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint@8395dad6b7d5d7d2e1d016cac1eede33ab404a3c # v2026.06.18
```

The inline justifications ("to comment on pull requests", "to comment on issues") are copied from `.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml:27-32`, where a `pull_request` trigger makes them correct. Here there is no PR to comment on. The composite action confirms it degrades to the push case — it resolves its ref as `${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}`, taking the `github.sha` branch.

`contents: read` is also stated as "required to checkout the repository", but this job has no checkout step; the composite action performs its own.

## Impact

The release pipeline's first job runs a MegaLinter composite action with a token that can write to every issue and pull request in the repository, for no reachable purpose. That widens the blast radius of the one job in this pipeline that executes third-party linter code, immediately before the job holding `secrets.PAT` and npm publish rights. The stale comments also mislead the next reader into treating the grants as load-bearing.

## Fix

Reduce to what a push-triggered lint gate can use:

```yaml
  Linter:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read # required by the action's own checkout step
      statuses: write # required to report the lint status on the pushed commit
      packages: read # required to read packages metadata
```

If a run then fails because MegaLinter's auto-fix path (`APPLY_FIXES: all` in `.mega-linter.yml:6`) tries to open a PR, the correct fix is to disable auto-fix for this workflow rather than to restore the write scopes — a release gate should report, not rewrite the commit it is gating.

## Resolution
Dropped `issues: write` and `pull-requests: write` from the Linter job in .github/workflows/publish.yml, leaving contents: read, statuses: write, packages: read. Corrected the stale inline justification on contents:read (the job has no checkout step; ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint performs its own) and added a comment explaining that a push-only trigger has no PR or issue to comment on. actionlint clean. Not exercised on GitHub — if MegaLinter's APPLY_FIXES path turns out to need write scope, the right response is to disable auto-fix for the release gate rather than restore the grants.
title: Release pipeline's lint gate holds issues:write and pull-requests:write on a push-only trigger

body:
## Problem

`@types/node` is declared at `"*"` — accepting any version, including future majors — in a repository that contains no TypeScript, no type-checking step, and ships no type declarations.

## Evidence

`package.json:48-51`:

```json
"devDependencies": {
  "@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config": "^2.0.7",
  "@types/node": "*"
}
```

Nothing consumes it. The repository has no `.ts` file (`git ls-files` lists `index.cjs`, `wrapper.mjs`, `scripts/postinstall.cjs`, `test/resolve.test.mjs` as the only sources), no `tsconfig.json`, no `types` or `typings` field in `package.json`, and `scripts` contains only `postinstall` and `test`:

```json
"scripts": {
  "postinstall": "node scripts/postinstall.cjs",
  "test": "node --test"
}
```

The v1 findings file records the sibling cleanup already applied — `[NIT-6] peerDependencies.typescript >=4 is spurious for a JSON config` — leaving this entry as the remaining half of the same mistake.

`"*"` is separately unsafe as a range: it is the only dependency in this file not bounded by a major, so `@types/node` v30 would be accepted without a Renovate PR or a lockfile review.

## Impact

Every `yarn install` in this repository and in CI downloads a package nothing reads, and the unbounded range means the version can change silently under a lockfile refresh. Reviewers reading `devDependencies` are told the project does typed development, which it does not.

## Fix

Delete it:

```json
"devDependencies": {
  "@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config": "^2.0.7"
}
```

Verify nothing depended on it with `node --test` and `yarn install --immutable`.

If editor IntelliSense over the `.cjs` files is the actual motivation, that is a per-developer concern, not a project dependency — a `jsconfig.json` with `"checkJs": false` and a globally installed `@types/node` covers it without a manifest entry. If instead the project wants type checking, that is a deliberate addition: pin the range (`"^26.0.0"`, matching `.nvmrc`), add a `typecheck` script, and gate it in `.github/workflows/test.yml`.

## Resolution
Removed the `@types/node: "*"` devDependency. Nothing consumed it — no .ts sources, no tsconfig.json, no `types` field, no typecheck script — and the wildcard was the only unbounded range in the manifest. Verified with `yarn install` followed by the full suite (8/8 passing); yarn's resolution step confirmed @types/node and undici-types dropping out of the tree.
title: @types/node is an unused wildcard devDependency in a package with no TypeScript

## Problem

The `resolutions` block pins three transitive packages that `git log` shows were added in response to advisories. `resolutions` is a Yarn-specific field that applies only when *this* repository installs; it is inert in the published package. The security posture it appears to provide does not reach consumers.

## Evidence

`package.json:52-56`:

```json
"resolutions": {
  "brace-expansion": "^5.0.6",
  "picomatch": "^4.0.4",
  "undici": "^8.0.0"
}
```

Provenance from `git log --oneline`:

```
5285c6c chore(deps): update dependency undici (8.0.2 → 8.5.0) [security] (#163)
06002e7 chore(deps): bump brace-expansion from 5.0.5 to 5.0.6 (#157)
109cee5 chore(deps): bump brace-expansion from 5.0.5 to 5.0.6 (#154)
```

npm and pnpm ignore `resolutions` entirely — the equivalents are `overrides` and `pnpm.overrides` — and no package manager applies a dependency's `resolutions` to the consuming project. A consumer installing `@ivuorinen/commitlint-config` gets whatever their own resolver picks for these transitives.

Two of the three pins have already gone stale inside this repository, which the lockfile finding in this run documents: `brace-expansion` is locked at 5.0.6 against three advisories fixed in 5.0.7/5.0.8/5.0.9, and `undici` at 8.5.0 is flagged by `osv-scanner`. A caret range does not pull a fix on its own — the lockfile has to be refreshed.

## Impact

No live exposure to consumers beyond what the direct dependency ranges already imply — this is recorded so the pins are not mistaken for a consumer-facing control. The practical risk is the opposite of protection: the block reads as "these CVEs are handled", so the lockfile drift that actually matters goes unreviewed. That is precisely what happened here.

## Fix

Keep the pins — they are correct for this repository's own install — but stop treating them as the control. Two changes:

1. Add the lockfile scan from the lockfile finding to `.github/workflows/test.yml`, so drift fails CI rather than relying on a range that only takes effect when the lock is regenerated.
2. Record what the block is for, since `package.json` cannot carry comments — in `README.md` or a `docs/` note:

```markdown
### Dependency pins

`resolutions` in `package.json` pins transitives with published advisories for
this repository's own install tree only. Yarn-specific, and not inherited by
consumers of the published package — consumers resolve transitives themselves
from the `dependencies` ranges. Re-check with
`osv-scanner scan source --lockfile=yarn.lock` after any lockfile change.
```

Drop a pin once the advisory's fix is inside the range that the direct dependency itself requires.

## Resolution
Pins kept — they are correct for this repository's own install tree, and the lockfile refresh confirmed it (brace-expansion resolved to 5.0.9 under the existing `^5.0.6`). Added a "Dependency pins" section to README.md recording that `resolutions` is Yarn-specific, applies to this repository only, is not inherited by consumers, and that the real gate is the osv-scanner step now running in .github/workflows/test.yml, with the local command to reproduce it. Table of Contents updated.
title: resolutions pins are Yarn-only and do not protect consumers of the published package

body:
## Problem

The release job caches `node_modules` keyed on the lockfile hash alone and skips `yarn install` on a hit. The Node version that built the cache is not part of the key, and `.nvmrc` is bumped frequently in this repository.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/publish.yml:69-79`:

```yaml
      - name: Cache Node Modules
        uses: actions/cache@2c8a9bd7457de244a408f35966fab2fb45fda9c8 # v6.0.0
        id: cache
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: node-modules-${{ hashFiles('**/yarn.lock') }}

      - name: Install Dependencies
        shell: bash
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: yarn install
```

`.nvmrc` moves independently of `yarn.lock` — four bumps in the recent history alone:

```
4726aeb chore(deps): update node.js (v26.3.1 → v26.4.0) (#168)
7141b1a chore(deps): update node.js (v24.16.0 → v24.17.0) (#164)
fd63e03 chore(deps): update node.js (v24.15.0 → v24.16.0) (#155)
```

A `.nvmrc`-only commit leaves the lockfile hash unchanged, so the cache hits, `yarn install` is skipped, and the release runs against a `node_modules` populated under the previous Node.

## Impact

No live failure today: the dependency tree is pure JavaScript, so a `node_modules` built under one Node major works under another. This is recorded as a latent condition rather than a defect — the day a transitive dependency ships a native binding or a postinstall that compiles against the Node ABI, the release job silently publishes from a tree built for the wrong runtime, and the skipped install means nothing revalidates it. The `runs-on` image is likewise absent from the key.

## Fix

Put the inputs that determine the cache's validity into its key:

```yaml
      - name: Cache Node Modules
        uses: actions/cache@2c8a9bd7457de244a408f35966fab2fb45fda9c8 # v6.0.0
        id: cache
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: node-modules-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('.nvmrc', '**/yarn.lock') }}
```

`actions/setup-node` also has built-in Yarn caching (`cache: yarn`) that caches the Yarn store rather than `node_modules` and always runs the install, which removes the skip-install branch entirely. Either is correct; the second is less to maintain.

## Resolution
Cache key in .github/workflows/publish.yml is now `node-modules-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('.nvmrc', '**/yarn.lock') }}`, so a .nvmrc-only bump invalidates the cache instead of reusing a tree built under the previous Node. Comment records why both inputs are in the key given that the install is skipped on a hit. actionlint clean; not exercised on GitHub.
title: node_modules cache key omits the Node version while .nvmrc changes often

## Problem

The install step added to the test workflow ran `yarn install --immutable`. Yarn 2+ executes package lifecycle scripts by default, so every dependency in the tree could run arbitrary code on the runner during install.

## Evidence

The step as first written, `.github/workflows/test.yml`:

```yaml
      - name: Install Dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: yarn install --immutable
```

SonarCloud rule `githubactions:S6505`, medium severity, on that line:

```
JavaScript package manager scripts should not be executed during installation
Lifecycle scripts are enabled by default in Yarn v2+.
```

This was introduced by this branch. The workflow previously ran `node --test` on a bare checkout with no install at all, so there was no lifecycle-script surface to flag until the new tests required real dependencies.

## Impact

A compromised or typosquatted transitive dependency gains arbitrary code execution on the test runner. The blast radius is smaller than the release job — this workflow's job holds only `contents: read` and no secrets — but it runs on every pull request, including from forks, which makes it the most frequently executed install in the repository.

## Fix

Skip build and lifecycle scripts; nothing in this tree needs them:

```yaml
      # The postinstall and commitlint tests load real dependencies, so the
      # suite no longer runs on a bare checkout. --mode=skip-build keeps
      # dependency lifecycle scripts from executing on the runner; nothing here
      # needs a build step, and the tests invoke this package's own postinstall
      # directly rather than relying on install to have run it.
      - name: Install Dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: yarn install --immutable --mode=skip-build
```

Verified locally: `yarn install --immutable --mode=skip-build` completes the link step and the full suite still passes 8/8, because `@commitlint/cli` and `@ivuorinen/config-checker` are pure JavaScript with no build step, and `test/postinstall.test.mjs` spawns the script itself rather than depending on install having run it.

## Resolution
Install step is now `yarn install --immutable --mode=skip-build`. Verified locally that the link step completes and the suite still passes 8/8 under that mode.
title: CI install ran dependency lifecycle scripts on the runner
